01. Qualified Candidates must be either be currently registered with the California Board of Behavioral Sciences (BBS). Please select what you currently hold and attach a copy along with your application. Options: Associate Marriage and Family Therapist | Associate Clinical Social Worker | Associate Professional Clinical Counselor | I am not currently registered with the California Board of Behavioral Sciences

02. To be fully evaluated as a qualified candidate for this position, you must submit the supplemental questionnaire. Options: Yes, I will attach the required supplemental questionnaire found at https://tinyurl.com/ClinicianPVSD | No, I will not be attaching the supplemental questionnaire, and understand that my application will be considered incomplete.
Maintain District standards of excellent customer service and professional behavior in various and sometimes challenging situations.
Access and monitor District email daily to receive important updates from school and District administration.
Participate in staff development and in-service training programs as assigned.
Conduct clinical intake assessments and prepare diagnostic evaluations, including gathering personal, social, emotional, and substance use histories.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams (e.g., IEP teams), families, and students to develop, implement, and evaluate goal-oriented treatment plans and provide case management.
Provide individual, group, and family therapy to support emotional and behavioral development and improve interpersonal and academic functioning.
Respond to crises by intervening when students exhibit acute psychiatric symptoms that may pose a danger to themselves or others.
Implement safe and appropriate proactive and responsive techniques in compliance with district policies and training to protect the safety and well-being of students and staff when required.
Offer outreach to community resources and supports families in navigating and applying for public assistance programs, such as Medi-Cal.
Consult with school personnel regarding students' mental health histories, treatment plans, and available community resources.
Collaborate with outside agencies and providers to coordinate care for students
Prepare documentation, including progress notes, treatment plans, and related correspondence
Work closely with health care, social service agencies, and community organizations to support the child and family.

Perform billing procedures for mental health services, including accurately completing Medi-Cal documentation, utilizing claims systems, applying appropriate service coding, and maintaining precise records of billable hours.
Participate in professional development and training related to clinical practices, cultural competency, compliance, co-occurring disorders and substance abuse.
Drive to various locations as needed to perform job duties and support students’ emotional and behavioral well-being.
Maintain electronic health records to support electronic billing.
May be assigned out of class work as prescribed by Merit Rules and Regulations.
